messages:
maria: heads up — cert-signing proxy started returning 403s for cert-request in ap-south nonprod about 09:03 UTC. observed after rbac change last night.

sanjay: logs?

maria: ```
[2026-03-20T09:03:12Z] cert-proxy ERROR signing failed: KMS ReEncryptDenied: Access denied for key arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:123456789012:key/abcd-1234
status=403 request_id=xyz-09-03-12
```

ben: that's the KMS deny, likely missing kms:ReEncryptFrom or kms:ReEncryptTo in the role/key policy or the proxy is assuming the wrong identity. which change was deployed?

maria: we applied org-rbac:serviceaccount-to-kms role binding for `cert-signer` -> `kms-rewrap-role` at 02:00 UTC. rollout script shows success but no post-deploy tests.

kelly: @ops-oncall can you check audit logs for AssumeRole and the KMS deny entries? need to confirm which principal was denied.

ops-oncall: checking cloudtrail: saw AssumeRole for svc-cert@ap-south at 02:01 then a cluster of kms:ReEncryptFrom events at 09:03 returned "AccessDenied". principal in deny entries is `sa/envoy` (svc-envoy) not `svc-cert`. that suggests proxy identity is doing the rewrap.

maria: right — signing flow: client -> cert-proxy (envoy) -> signing-svc. previously signing-svc used its own role to call KMS. RBAC tweak changed the caller identity flow so the proxy's SA is used for the rewrap.

sanjay: so two issues: (1) envoy SA lost permission to call signing-svc (ingress RBAC), (2) envoy SA doesn't have ReEncrypt permissions on the KMS key. signing-svc used to own the KMS call.

ben: quick mitigation options: revert last night's RBAC binding (fast), or patch key policy to allow envoy SA temporarily (riskier). which has lower blast radius?

kelly: revert RBAC is lower blast radius. initiating rollback now.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated: org-rbac-change-20260320 by kelly — step 1/3

maria: while rollback is in progress, can we patch signing-svc to explicitly assume its own role before doing the rewrap? that would decouple identity from the upstream caller.

sanjay: agree — implement STS assume-role in signing-svc rewrap path and fall back to local key if assume fails. open ticket and schedule after stabilization.

ops-oncall: rollback complete. Connectivity check: cert exchange tests passing again for ap-south nonprod at 09:18 UTC. no successful rewraps recorded during the deny window.

maria: good. audit logs for the 15-minute window are a bit sparse — some request IDs missing from ingestion. need to confirm no certs were minted with legacy/weak ciphers while this was happening.

kelly: running quick CloudTrail query: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --start-time 2026-03-20T09:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-20T09:30:00Z --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=ReEncryptFrom` — will paste results shortly.

maria: found 12 ReEncryptFrom attempts; 4 are denied, 8 were from the signing-svc once rollback finished. No successful rewraps while denied. still worth rotating any certs if we see odd signatures.

ben: vuln triage note: separate scanner yesterday flagged TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20 (legacy clients) on an older canary pod in eu-west. unrelated but increases urgency to run a targeted cipher/PKI scan.

sanjay: recommend opening an incident ticket. set priority P2 until we confirm no weak-signed certs were issued. tag infra+sec.

maria: filing incident INC-20260320-1, attaching logs, RBAC change diff, and rollback timeline.

sec-bot: incident created INC-20260320-1 by maria. priority=P2. linked playbook: cert-signing-rbac-failure-v1

kelly: immediate action items: 
1) postmortem of RBAC deploy (owner: infra)
2) add integration test asserting signing-proxy identity mapping and KMS behavior in CI (owner: devex)
3) implement signing-svc assume-role fallback for KMS calls (owner: eng-runtime)
4) update keypolicy automation to include proxy identities or enforce explicit assume-role model (owner: security)

ops-oncall: alerts added: CloudTrail AccessDenied spikes for KMS keys (threshold: >3/min) and cert-proxy 5xx rate >1% triggers paging.

maria: also need a short-runbook: how to rollback RBAC quickly, how to add temporary keypolicy allow, and how to validate signing path end-to-end (curl + openssl s_client + CSR acceptance). I'll put a draft in confluence.

sanjay: i'll start the PR to add `kms:ReEncryptFrom` mapping for envoy SA where appropriate and include a guardrail script that flags when an identity can trigger a rewrap without assume-role.

ben: schedule targeted TLS cipher scan across regions: priorities AP-SOUTH, EU-WEST, US-EAST. ops please run and share results.

maria: thanks all. thread resolved for now — reopen if any followup. :white_check_mark:
